symptom: On Windows with Docker Desktop, `mxcli mcp capabilities -p App.mpr --mcp http://localhost:7782/mcp` failed with `dial tcp <LAN IP>:7782: i/o timeout` while Studio Pro listened on 127.0.0.1; `--mcp-dial 127.0.0.1:7782` connected. The reporter blamed localhost resolving to the LAN address (mendixlabs/mxcli#1684)
cause: mdl/backend/mcp/client.go rewrote a localhost/127.0.0.1 endpoint to host.docker.internal:<port> whenever net.LookupHost(host.docker.internal) succeeded, as a 'running in a devcontainer' test. Docker Desktop for Windows writes host.docker.internal into the host's own hosts file (the LAN IP), so the rewrite also fired on the host, for 127.0.0.1 URLs too
fix: Dial a plan instead of one address: an explicit --mcp-dial alone, otherwise the URL host first and host.docker.internal:<port> as the fallback when it resolves; every failure is reported when none connects
insight: 'A name resolves' is evidence about DNS, not about where the process runs; the same Docker name is injected into containers and into Windows hosts. Prefer trying the likely address and falling back over guessing the environment: a refused loopback connection in a container costs nothing. The address in the error (a LAN IP for a localhost URL) pointed at the rewrite, not at localhost resolution. Test it by forcing the cached 'resolves' answer true and connecting to a loopback fake
